scenario_or_breakage: Repo-root, larch-logs, dirty-tree, and main-branch guards are listed but not ordered, and edge case 463 only forbids mutation on a dirty tree for non-dry-run
suggested_fix: An implementer can run `--dry-run` on a dirty or non-main tree, or defer guards until the apply block, breaking SKILL.md NEVER rules and the bash pre-scan refusal path Add an explicit pre-scan guard sequence matching bash: flag parse → `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` → `larch-logs/` exists → clean porcelain → branch is `main`; state these checks run before enumeration and before any `--dry-run` exit; reword edge case 463 to say guards apply to dry-run and apply alike

scenario_or_breakage: Apply path says "Stage, commit, push" without scoping staging to `larch-logs/` only
suggested_fix: Bash uses `git add -A -- "$LOGS_ROOT/"`; a repo-wide `git add -A` could commit unrelated tracked changes if guard timing or porcelain semantics drift Say staging must be `git add -A -- <repo_root>/larch-logs/` (or equivalent path-limited add) before commit, matching bash line 344

scenario_or_breakage: Plan mentions quiet helpers but not `quiet_init`/`diagnostic`/`emit_kv` wiring for the KV contract
suggested_fix: Bash routes machine KVs through fd 3 after `larch_quiet_init`; diagnostics use `larch_err`. Without `logging_util.quiet_init(argv0=...)` before `emit_kv` and `diagnostic()` for skip/plan lines, KVs can mix with operator text and break `/gc-run-logs` stdout parsing In `python/gc_run_logs.py`, require `quiet_init` at CLI entry (after argv validation), `emit_kv` for all contract keys, and `diagnostic()` for per-dir skip/plan messages; note pytest must cover fd-3 separation per migration playbook

scenario_or_breakage: Plan does not require pinning every git/gh call to the resolved repo root
suggested_fix: Bash always uses `git -C "$REPO_ROOT"` after top-level resolution; cwd-relative git during apply could target the wrong repo if invoked outside the consumer checkout Say resolve `repo_root` once and pass it as `cwd`/`git -C` for status, log date fallback, branch checkout, add, commit, and push; route subprocesses through `proc.run` so tests can stub safely

scenario_or_breakage: Tests mention monkeypatchable runner boundaries but the module section does not require an injectable seam
suggested_fix: Implementer may use bare `subprocess.run`, making push/PR stubs brittle; tests still pass if they monkeypatch at module level Add optional `Runner`/proc injection only if pytest proves hard to stub without it
